Cavernous earth

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It is a danger zone... and it stinks. The streets of small towns on the far west Rand are like scenes from a post apocalyptic thriller..

Unique Selling Point:
It is a matter of time, before the earth swallows parts of the Gauteng West Rand... the only solution is for residents to move far away... but where will they go?
Residents of Khutsong on the Gauteng West Rand have been living in a danger zone for years, partly because of century long mining activities, but mostly due to neglect... and the blame lies at the door of the Merafong Municipality.

Summary:
The yawning cavities in the earth, breathe out a stench that lingers for days…The streets of Khutsong on the far West Rand are like scenes from a post-apocalyptic thriller. Life here, has become dreadful and residents live with constant fear of knowing; the earth may swallow them at any given time. But they stay because they have nowhere else to go.
The entire far West Rand should be declared a national disaster but pleas from the Human Rights Commission have fallen on death ears, just like some residents here, have fallen into gaping holes caused by rising levels of raw sewage.


Further information:
The total collapse of the entire sewage system of the Merafong municipality has become a situation of life and death. Raw sewage is filling the earth that has been hollowed out by more than a century of gold mining activities. But this, is not a mining problem, it’s a municipal disaster. A lack of maintenance and upgrades to the sewage systems have now resulted in rivers of raw sewage running down most streets and sidewalks. But Khutsong is only one of many towns affected in the greater Merafong municipal area.
Between Randfontein and Westonaria, a canal has formed, running for over 20 kilometers next to the main road.
The sewage is eating away at the sides of the road, and large chunks of tar and cement road have broken off, causing ravine-like cracks and potholes. The municipality is merely filling them up with gravel.
Merafong municipality on the West Rand of Gauteng includes towns like Carletonville, Fochville, Welverdiend and Khutsong. And it has lost complete control of every single sewerage plant in the district. Sewage is running everywhere.
The well-known one-meter pipeline that runs parallel to the R28 between Randfontein and Westonaria, was constructed to carry sewage away from residential areas. No sewage was supposed to end up on the vast landscape between Randfontein and Westonaria because the dolomite is so sensitive that the earth will disintegrate in the presence of any acidic liquid. The one-meter pipeline has not been maintained, and two large sewage dams have formed, right here, where it was declared a danger zone more than 50 years ago. Reports with analysis, warnings and recommendations have been handed to the municipality since 2009 with the latest one released in 2021. But not one recommendation was adhered to and now it seems the situations is irreversible. The sewage levels are so high and blockages in pipes so many that it pumps raw sewage back into pipelines bubbling out in people’s backyards, from where it forms river and dams and eventually sinkholes so big, that an entire house can fit into them.
Every stream, river and water canal have been polluted and dirty water runs from the West Rand to the Boskopdam that supplies drinking water to Potchefstroom and then it finally ends up in the Vaal dam.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It is a danger zone... and it stinks. The streets of small towns on the far west Rand are like scenes from a post apocalyptic thriller..
metadata.Unique Selling Point: It is a matter of time, before the earth swallows parts of the Gauteng West Rand... the only solution is for residents to move far away... but where will they go? Residents of Khutsong on the Gauteng West Rand have been living in a danger zone for years, partly because of century long mining activities, but mostly due to neglect... and the blame lies at the door of the Merafong Municipality.
metadata.Summary: The yawning cavities in the earth, breathe out a stench that lingers for days…The streets of Khutsong on the far West Rand are like scenes from a post-apocalyptic thriller. Life here, has become dreadful and residents live with constant fear of knowing; the earth may swallow them at any given time. But they stay because they have nowhere else to go. The entire far West Rand should be declared a national disaster but pleas from the Human Rights Commission have fallen on death ears, just like some residents here, have fallen into gaping holes caused by rising levels of raw sewage.
metadata.Further information: The total collapse of the entire sewage system of the Merafong municipality has become a situation of life and death. Raw sewage is filling the earth that has been hollowed out by more than a century of gold mining activities. But this, is not a mining problem, it’s a municipal disaster. A lack of maintenance and upgrades to the sewage systems have now resulted in rivers of raw sewage running down most streets and sidewalks. But Khutsong is only one of many towns affected in the greater Merafong municipal area. Between Randfontein and Westonaria, a canal has formed, running for over 20 kilometers next to the main road. The sewage is eating away at the sides of the road, and large chunks of tar and cement road have broken off, causing ravine-like cracks and potholes. The municipality is merely filling them up with gravel. Merafong municipality on the West Rand of Gauteng includes towns like Carletonville, Fochville, Welverdiend and Khutsong. And it has lost complete control of every single sewerage plant in the district. Sewage is running everywhere. The well-known one-meter pipeline that runs parallel to the R28 between Randfontein and Westonaria, was constructed to carry sewage away from residential areas. No sewage was supposed to end up on the vast landscape between Randfontein and Westonaria because the dolomite is so sensitive that the earth will disintegrate in the presence of any acidic liquid. The one-meter pipeline has not been maintained, and two large sewage dams have formed, right here, where it was declared a danger zone more than 50 years ago. Reports with analysis, warnings and recommendations have been handed to the municipality since 2009 with the latest one released in 2021. But not one recommendation was adhered to and now it seems the situations is irreversible. The sewage levels are so high and blockages in pipes so many that it pumps raw sewage back into pipelines bubbling out in people’s backyards, from where it forms river and dams and eventually sinkholes so big, that an entire house can fit into them. Every stream, river and water canal have been polluted and dirty water runs from the West Rand to the Boskopdam that supplies drinking water to Potchefstroom and then it finally ends up in the Vaal dam.
